themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes piling up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned Bike complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 700% increase (z-score: 4.95)—suggesting either a sudden dumping problem or a breakdown in removal services in CD 314.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 average per week over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
No contextual Reddit or news coverage yet—emerging signal
reporting_angles: Are bike-share companies (Citi Bike, others) failing to retrieve damaged bikes from streets in Midwood/Ocean Parkway?
Is there a new illegal dumping site or theft-for-parts operation targeting bikes in the district?

themes_detail.label: Street signs damaged across district
themes_detail.summary: Street Sign - Damaged complaints reached 7 THIS WEEK, a 522% surge from the 1.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.64), indicating possible concentrated vandalism, weather damage, or vehicle collisions affecting wayfinding and safety.
evidence: 7 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 average per week over prior 8 weeks (522% increase, z-score: 3.64)
Concentrated spike suggests a specific incident or pattern rather than chronic wear
May intersect with litter basket and graffiti spikes, indicating broader public space degradation
reporting_angles: Did a single weather event (high wind, storm) cause widespread sign damage this week?
Is there a specific neighborhood block or corridor experiencing vandalism or vehicle damage?

themes_detail.label: Litter baskets inadequate
themes_detail.summary: Litter Basket Requests jumped to 4 THIS WEEK from a 1.4 weekly average—a 191% spike (z-score: 3.77)—suggesting residents perceive insufficient waste receptacles, particularly in light of concurrent graffiti and street sign damage complaints indicating broader sanitation concerns.
evidence: 4 litter basket requests THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 average per week over prior 8 weeks (191% increase, z-score: 3.77)
Converges with Graffiti spike (10 complaints last week, 248% above baseline) and Dirty Condition complaints (488 total in 90 days)
May correlate with ongoing rezoning activity (1455 Coney Island Ave, 2586 Nostrand Ave, 1584 Flatbush Ave) attracting foot traffic
reporting_angles: Which neighborhoods or commercial corridors lack adequate waste receptacles? Map the litter basket request locations.
Is increased street activity from development projects outpacing sanitation capacity?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge spreading
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints reached 10 LAST WEEK, a 248% increase from the 2.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.23)—a sustained and statistically severe spike indicating either a coordinated tagging campaign or degradation of removal response times in CD 314.
evidence: 10 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 average per week over prior 8 weeks (248% increase, z-score: 5.23)
Converges with Street Sign - Damaged spike (7 THIS WEEK) and Litter Basket Request spike (4 THIS WEEK), suggesting coordinated public space degradation
No Reddit or local news coverage yet, suggesting under-reported community concern
reporting_angles: Is there a specific crew or gang responsible for coordinated tagging across Midwood, Ditmas Park, or Ocean Parkway zones?
How quickly is NYPD or city agencies responding to graffiti removal requests? Are complaints piling up faster than removal crews can handle?

themes_detail.label: Elevator failures accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 26 LAST WEEK, a 117% increase from the 12.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.59)—a significant spike affecting building safety and mobility, especially given CD 314's aging multifamily housing stock with 348 building permits filed recently.
evidence: 26 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.0 average per week over prior 8 weeks (117% increase, z-score: 3.59)
348 building alteration/renovation permits filed in last 90 days (268 alterations), many potentially affecting mechanical systems
Converges with Appliance complaints (29 two weeks ago, 150% above baseline, z-score: 3.57), suggesting broader mechanical system failures in aging buildings
reporting_angles: Are landlords deferring elevator maintenance during construction/renovation cycles, or are elevators failing due to age and lack of upkeep?
Interview residents in rent-stabilized or affordable buildings experiencing repeated elevator outages; investigate HPD enforcement against non-compliant landlords.
